items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5551

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to the powers
of the state of New York mortgage agency

 PURPOSE OF BILL :

The purpose of this proposed bill is to authorize State of New York
Mortgage Agency ("SONYMA") to (a) purchase second mortgage loans to
provide borrowers of SONYMA first mortgage loans with down payment
and/or closing cost assistance under certain limited circumstances,
and (b) to insure such second mortgage loans.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Bill §1 expands the definition of "mortgage" set forth in Public
Authorities Law ("PAL") §2402(5) to include mortgages secured by a
second lien in cases where the second lien: (i) secures a mortgage
loan purchased by SONYMA, and (ii) is made at the same time as a first
lien securing a mortgage loan purchased by SONYMA pursuant to its
programs or is made at the same time as a new housing loan purchased
by SONYMA pursuant to PAL §2405-c.

Bill §2 amends PAL §2402(5) as described in Bill §1 in the event of
the expiration of the amendment to PAL §2402(5) set forth in Bill §1.

Bill §3 amends PAL §2405(7)(e) to conform the definition of mortgage
as set forth in Bill §1 with respect to bank covenants to SONYMA in
connection with SONYMA's forward commitment program.

Bill §4 amends PAL §2405(7)(e) as described in Bill §3 in the event of
the expiration of the amendment to PAL §2405(7)(e) set forth in Bill
§3.

Bill §5 amends PAL §2405-b(8)(f) to conform the definition of mortgage
as set forth in Bill §1 with respect to bank covenants to SONYMA in
connection with SONYMA's purchase-out-of-portfolio program.

Bill §6 amends PAL §2428(4) to allow the Mortgage Insurance Fund (MIF)
to insure second mortgages purchased by SONYMA.

Bill §7 amends PAL §2428(4) as described in Bill §6 in the event of
the expiration of the amendment to PAL §2428(4) set forth in Bill §6.

Bill §8 provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

SONYMA does not currently have the authority to purchase mortgages for
second lien purposes or to insure such mortgages. Under the definition
of "mortgage" set forth in PAL §2402(5), the definition of mortgage in
SONYMA's programs is limited to mortgages secured by first liens.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

A9037 of the 2001/02 legislative session
A8029 of the 2003/04 legislative session
A8266 of the 2005/06 legislative session
A6999 of the 2007/08 legislative session

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

SONYMA is seeking the authority to purchase second mortgages in the
following limited circumstance: (1) the second mortgage secures a loan
purchased by SONYMA; (2) the second mortgage is made at the same time
and with respect to the same secured property as a first or senior
mortgage that is secured by a loan purchased by SONYMA pursuant to its
programs; and (3) the borrower shall contribute from his or her own
verifiable funds an amount not less than such percentage as the Agency
shall determine, of the lower of the purchase price or appraised value
of the property subject to the first lien. It has been a requirement
of SONYMA's programs that eligible borrowers contribute from his or
her own verifiable funds an amount not less than three percent of the
lower of the purchase price or appraised value of the property subject
to the first lien.

This amendment will permit SONYMA to more efficiently structure
programs which feature closing cost and or down-payment assistance to
borrowers whose underlying mortgage loans are financed by SONYMA under
its various programs. Down-payment and closing cost assistance-type
programs would represent an important adjunct of SONYMA's below market
interest rate financing and are intended to address the critical
problem of the limited cash resources available to otherwise qualified
low and moderate income SONYMA applicants.

This amendment would facilitate the operation of SONYMA products which
which have provided closing cost and/or down payment assistance to
low-income first time home buyers with limited cash reserves. These
loans would be secured by a second lien on the homeowner's property.

SONYMA's flexibility in offering these programs is currently hindered
by the fact that SONYMA has no statutory authority to offer second
lien financing, except in connection with home improvement loans. This
forces SONYMA to configure its down-payment or closing cost assistance
programs using a burdensome and administratively cumbersome co-first
lien mortgage structure. Such a structure adds unnecessary complexity
which is confusing to many borrowers, county clerks and lenders.  In
some cases, county clerks have refused to record such instruments
unless altered to their satisfaction.  Also, because the co-first lien
and the underlying first mortgage have different term lengths,
extinguishing the co-first lien at maturity has proved troublesome.
As such, borrowers have difficulty obtaining second and home equity
mortgages due to the co-first lien not being removed from the public
record.  Additionally, the legal and procedural complexities inherent
in structuring co-first mortgage arrangements makes it more difficult
for SONYMA to put together and manage.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediate upon passage of the bill.

summary: Provides that the term "mortgage" shall also include a loan owed to a bank secured by a second lien on a fee simple or leasehold estate in real property located in the state and improved by a residential structure, whether or not insured or guaranteed by the United States of America or any agency thereof, provided, however, that such second lien secures a loan purchased by the agency and is made at the same time as a first lien securing a loan purchased by the agency.
title: Provides that the term "mortgage" shall also include a loan owed to a bank secured by a second lien on a fee simple or leasehold estate in real property located in the state
